A close reading for the week

“Juliet is the sun”

Romeo and Juliet · Act 2, Scene 2

Romeo believes he is describing Juliet. He is largely describing his own way of loving: a rhetoric of light, worship and distance that the rest of the scene, and Juliet herself, will put under pressure.

But soft,1 what light through yonder window breaks?
It is the east, and Juliet is the sun!2

  1. 1

    A whisper that opens a flood

    “Soft” here means wait, be quiet. Romeo hushes himself, then delivers some of the most unrestrained praise in the play. The little self-interruption reminds us that he is trespassing in the Capulet orchard, where being heard could cost his life.

  2. 2

    Not “like” the sun

    Romeo makes an identification where a comparison might be expected. Juliet is the sun, and the window becomes the east. The grammar matters: a simile keeps two things separate, while this metaphor rebuilds the world so that Juliet stands at its centre and everything else (moon, stars, night) must adjust around her.
